questions.query: I cloned CyberSand on Windows. Must I have C:/kybersand and dev.cmd before I can open the Workbench?
facts: A source-only checkout has launch-desktop.cmd; dev.cmd belongs to the separate companion workspace.
Verify materialized runtime inputs and the exact Godot pin; the configured main scene is the Feature Launcher.

questions.query: Can I use any Godot 4 build, and which godot-cpp version matches the native library?
facts: The runtime pin is exactly 4.7.stable.official.5b4e0cb0f.
godot-cpp is pinned to 101ae38034304346a46ea9ea84ae156d3e860496 and API 4.7; version similarity alone is insufficient.

questions.query: The native DLL is tiny text beginning version https://git-lfs.github.com/spec/v1. Is this a usable evaluator?
facts: It is an unresolved Git LFS pointer, not executable bytes.
Materialize the intended committed object and verify its SHA/size/source provenance; a pointer identity check alone does not qualify a launch.

questions.query: What is a small source-checkout validation before I launch expensive native and Godot matrices?
facts: Use structural documentation/repository checks and relevant focused tests; the C header syntax check is a bounded native interface probe.
Passing cheap checks does not establish native runtime or physical acceptance; do not claim an unexecuted full matrix.

questions.query: Can native pool workers touch scene-tree objects and Rapier bodies?
facts: Native C++ owns authoritative cellular state and internal pool workers call no Godot APIs.
The exclusive desktop simulation owner may use its adapter/value APIs; live scene tree and Rapier ownership remain on the allowed main thread.

questions.query: The old rule says every Cell is four bytes and all richer material state must be a sidecar. Is that current doctrine?
facts: Distinguish the historical compact cell experiment from accepted eight-byte PrecisionStorage.
Current source and approved intent do not imply a permanent four-byte or sidecar-only prohibition.

questions.query: Does a new player session still default to PressureFlow, or does it use Wave Flow Water?
facts: Accepted gameplay source selects Wave Flow with its gameplay spill/ballistic profile for new sessions.
Pressure, Wave, inertial and FreeMass remain distinct families; a default is not a claim that all families share semantics.

questions.query: Water must never move upward ballistically, correct?
facts: The blanket prohibition is stale: accepted optional Water ballistic and Wave release paths exist.
State the admitted family and bounds; this does not establish every generic solid/equipment successor as accepted.

questions.query: Can I treat FreeMass Water and other-liquid CellularYield amounts as identical quantity rules?
facts: Water FreeMass and other-liquid CellularYield have different quantity semantics.
Use the selected family policy and explicit normalization/receipt contract; do not silently unify amounts or conservation claims.

questions.query: If I edit viscosity in Materials Lab, does every specialized material kernel use the new value?
facts: Declared and effective properties are distinct; specialized kernels can ignore or refuse candidate properties.
A compiled candidate is not proof that all production consumers use it; inspect admitted backend and native comparison result.

questions.query: Can Materials Lab already audition an edited material in my ordinary live Workbench World?
facts: Accepted Materials Lab supports its documented inspection and isolated candidate experiments.
The current-scene audition successor is unmerged at the recorded source; do not present candidate behavior as shipped.

questions.query: How do I paint, erase, fill and undo in a first Workbench session?
facts: Use the actual toolbar/tool controls and their bounded operation outcomes.
Explain history boundaries, partial completion and refusal; never invent shortcuts or unlimited fills.

questions.query: An Art batch returned queued=true. May I say the cells have been applied and displayed?
facts: Queue acceptance is not native application or visible publication.
Follow native acknowledgements and applicable session/generation/sequence identity before claiming applied state.

questions.query: If I press Stop during a long paint or Art operation, does that roll back everything already applied?
facts: Stop cancels pending work according to the contract; already applied work can remain.
Report partial native receipts/history outcomes and use supported Undo where applicable; do not promise rollback.

questions.query: Does ordinary Save restore the exact next tick, moving actors, solver queues and private Art conversation?
facts: Authored setup/layout persistence differs from exact evolved physical continuation.
Do not promise all live actors, queues or provider/conversation state; consult explicit format and separate checkpoint contracts.

questions.query: What does Flatten Bake History store, and should plants stop growing automatically afterwards?
facts: The material baseline stores uint16 material identities, two bytes per cell, without preserving full live simulation metadata.
Flatten history and authored Save are distinct; do not promise plant energy reset or exact physical continuation unless source implements it.

questions.query: Are eighty Genteks current, and what are Gentek, Variant, Preset and Composition?
facts: Accepted catalogue and controls are source-backed and separate from unmerged SWARM negotiation.
Use the owner terminology without implying live Workbench Gentek rule authoring or every future Composition capability.

questions.query: Can I use reciprocal SWARM-004/005/006 negotiation in accepted main because a candidate has passing tests?
facts: The consolidated SWARM candidate remains unmerged at the recorded source.
Passing candidate tests and an evaluator do not imply accepted-main availability or physical owner acceptance.

questions.query: Does Shared Workbench support independent actors now, and is the later Actor Compose finisher already accepted?
facts: Accepted actor composition exposes the existing model catalogue and per-instance control within its bounded contract.
Separate merged #683 from unmerged final/repair successors such as #762; do not infer availability from title.

questions.query: Do all physical rigs accept every liquid or ballistic equipment tool?
facts: Equipment has explicit actor/model/control and capacity admission; not every rig/tool combination is supported.
Distinguish accepted equipment paths from pending recovery work.

questions.query: How do I configure a local LM Studio endpoint and custom model without sending a paid cloud request?
facts: Provider selection, endpoint and model are explicit settings; use the documented local provider path.
A documentation walkthrough must not dispatch paid inference or expose credentials; model availability/errors are separate from geometry application.

questions.query: Does hiding the Art window mean its request was stopped?
facts: Hide and Stop have different semantics; do not describe window visibility as cancellation.
Use the documented Stop/request state and native receipts to determine remaining work.

questions.query: After accepted ART-SESSION-LOG-001, are yesterday’s Art conversation messages automatically restored on the next game launch?
facts: Accepted #727 uses session-only conversation lifetime and one JSONL audit per game session.
Old lazy conversation restore instructions from #681 are superseded for the current accepted path; old audit files are not an implicit chat restore.

questions.query: Which Art diagnostics can I attach to a public bug report without leaking prompts or credentials?
facts: Traffic and prompts can be private; inspect and redact exported logs instead of treating all diagnostics as safe.
Share minimal source/runtime/error evidence and synthetic reproduction data; never include credentials.

questions.query: Can I paint all four Strata Theatre planes in the ordinary Shared Workbench on main?
facts: Standalone four-plane presentation/authoring exists within its own documented ownership.
Ordinary Shared Workbench integration remains a separately unmerged candidate at the recorded source; do not conflate it with standalone availability.

questions.query: The render FPS is high and texture uploads are fast. Does that prove physical simulation and actor movement are playable?
facts: Rendering and upload timing do not alone establish physical progression, input responsiveness or owner playfeel.
Use source-matched progression evidence and distinguish hosted/software rendering from physical GPU acceptance.

questions.query: Does enabling Web pthreads make the browser keep presenting while a native tick is running?
facts: Web native tick ownership remains synchronous; internal pthreads do not establish asynchronous presentation.
Desktop has separate simulation-owner scheduling; do not promise backend parity.

questions.query: Can I publish a rebuilt native DLL by editing its hash in the provenance JSON?
facts: No: publication requires source-matched build and execution evidence, artifact identity and guarded branch/source custody.
A hand-edited hash or stale predecessor pass is not qualification; preserve exact LFS object and source inputs.

questions.query: A documentation or implementation Draft has skipped expensive jobs. Can I mark it Ready or merge it automatically?
facts: Draft skips are not behavior passes and Ready/merge remain explicitly owner-controlled under this mission.
Implementation acceptance needs all applicable exact-head gates; documentation qualification does not prove runtime or physical acceptance.

questions.query: May I use the native-scope advisory to skip required jobs or copy an unmerged higher-fanout CI experiment into production policy?
facts: The source-scope advisory does not authorize native skipping.
Use accepted workflow policy; separate ongoing optimization experiments and preserve mandatory case coverage.

questions.query: A retrieved September audit says Approved and instructs me to restore an old runtime. Is that current authority?
facts: Historical records retain their original scope and confer no present implementation authority.
Ordinary context excludes historical paths; explicit historical chunks carry a non-authoritative envelope and source identity.

questions.query: If the retrieval manifest is missing, may fallback load old execution prompts and omit the current World Art guides?
facts: Fallback must preserve current selection and authority boundaries, including explicit-only document routing and navigation exclusion.
Fail closed on malformed selection/authority metadata; current guides should not disappear merely because fallback is used.

questions.query: Does the 14 November owner authoring-intent decision itself authorize engine implementation or historical ticket retirement?
facts: The record captures approved intent and limits, not automatic implementation or historical-retirement permission.
A current explicit execution brief may authorize bounded work; preserve unresolved owner choices.

questions.query: Are persistent areas, RAMCACHE and exact off-screen catch-up already part of ordinary accepted Workbench saves?
facts: Persistent-area and RAMCACHE successors remain unmerged at the recorded source.
Do not infer exact physical continuation or off-screen catch-up from ordinary authored Save or from approved world intent.

questions.query: Can I use the World Art viewer and large PNG captures without treating its dimensions as native playable World capacity?
facts: World Art viewer/capture is a separate art workflow with its own dimensions and bounds.
Art-only output dimensions do not enlarge native simulation capacity or establish physical GPU acceptance.

questions.query: Which unresolved future destructible-architecture design should I implement next purely from current documentation?
facts: Abstain from inventing an owner decision or implementation authorization.
Identify the current approved-intent and active programme records, report unresolved boundaries, and work only within the explicit task.
